name: MMVU
intro: MMVU 是专家级、多学科视频理解基准：论文报告 3,000 道题、1,529 个专业领域视频，覆盖科学、医疗健康、人文社会科学和工程四大核心学科的 27 个主题。专家依据权威教材定位动态概念，筛选经 YouTube Data API v3 核验的 CC 视频，编写选择题或开放题，并标注领域知识与逐步推理依据。论文将数据随机划分为 1,000 项验证集和 2,000 项测试集；当前仅验证集公开，测试标注隐藏并由作者运行提交代码。官方评测代码按题型让 GPT-4o 抽取答案并返回结构化正确性布尔值，解析失败记为错误。
build_method: 用户研究, 教材引导专家标注, CC视频筛选, 专家复核与修订
task_type: 视频选择题, 开放式问答
eval_feature: 视频必要性验证, 题型专用GPT-4o结构化判分, 解析失败记错
scale: 3,000个问题, 1,529个视频; 公开验证集1,000, 隐藏测试集2,000
build_method_en: User Study, Textbook-guided Expert Annotation, CC-video Filtering, Expert Review and Revision
eval_feature_en: Video-necessity validation, QA-type-specific structured GPT-4o grading, parse failures scored incorrect
intro_en: MMVU is an expert-level, multidisciplinary video-understanding benchmark. The paper reports 3,000 questions over 1,529 specialized-domain videos spanning 27 subjects in four core disciplines: Science, Healthcare, Humanities & Social Sciences, and Engineering. Experts use authoritative textbooks to identify dynamic concepts, select Creative Commons videos verified through YouTube Data API v3, author multiple-choice or open-ended questions, and annotate domain knowledge and step-by-step rationales. The paper randomly divides the benchmark into a 1,000-item validation split and a 2,000-item test split; only validation is currently public, while test annotations are hidden and submissions are run by the authors. The official evaluator asks GPT-4o to extract an answer and return a structured correctness Boolean by QA type, with parse failures scored incorrect.

drawio_review_note: Primary-source audit pinned the paper to arXiv:2501.12380v1, the official repository to commit 4d54223d912f498707c105ab645a921abce6e39a, and the public Hugging Face dataset to revision b937f414a87e9012acba49d95669020b24fa9ee9. Paper §3.1 supports the 133-person user study, two examples per participant, author selection of 27 subjects across four disciplines, protocol training, and at least two experts per subject. It contains an unresolved internal count conflict: §3.1 says 67 annotators (22 senior undergraduates, 36 graduate students, and nine authors), whereas Appendix A.1 Tables 4-5 enumerate IDs 1 through 73 and call them 73 annotators. The diagram preserves both claims instead of silently choosing one. Paper §3.2 supports expert-selected authoritative textbooks, chapter-by-chapter dynamic-concept discovery, YouTube Creative Commons video search, license verification through YouTube Data API v3, relevant timestamps recorded with each question, excluded audio tracks, minimal on-screen text, lecture exclusion, two or three questions per video, MCQ/open-ended routing, four plausible distractors plus one correct option, random option shuffling, Wikipedia-linked domain knowledge, and step-by-step rationale. The pinned repository README additionally says rationales were proofread by GPT-4o; this is shown as repository evidence, not substituted for the paper's expert-authorship claim. Paper §3.3 and Appendix A.4 support author or top-annotator validation, video-necessity checks against text-only and single-frame shortcuts, revision and resubmission, 523 revised examples, and 72 still-misaligned exclusions. The time-based compensation facts and 20m17s/4m12s averages come from §3.3 and Appendix A.5. Table 2 fixes the final snapshot at 3,000 questions over 1,529 videos, with 1,858 MCQ, 1,142 open-ended, 1,000 validation, and 2,000 test items. Section 3.4 says the split is random and the test set remains hidden. This is corroborated by the pinned repository README, which asks users to submit code for author-run testing, and by the pinned HF revision, which exposes only validation.json. Direct inspection of that revision counted exactly 1,000 rows: 625 multiple-choice and 375 open-ended; all 1,000 have non-empty rationale and knowledge fields even though the same pinned HF card still labels those fields ‘Coming Soon!’. The public-data observation therefore wins for field presence, while no completeness claim is made for the hidden 2,000 items. The repository and HF card declare no dataset license at the pinned revisions. Paper video selection is CC-licensed, but that source-video condition is not broadened into a dataset-license claim; the project website's CC BY-SA footer applies to the website. Paper §4.1 and Appendix B.1-B.2 support CoT/direct prompts, temperature 1.0, model-specific video or frame input, and a maximum of 1,024 tokens except 8,192 for Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking. At the pinned repository, utils/eval_utils.py uses separate MCQ and open-answer instructions, requests a Pydantic EvaluationOutput containing extracted_answer and correct, requires A-E for MCQ, and accepts an open answer only when it explicitly and unambiguously expresses the same technique or concept without inventing a missing answer. acc_evaluation.py and utils/api_utils.py call the unversioned gpt-4o alias, return None after a bad request or after ten total attempts for retryable failures, and map a missing/malformed structured result to an empty extracted answer and correct=False. Accuracy is the mean of those item Booleans. The official project page currently publishes a results leaderboard, so has_leaderboard is true, while its test submission system remains author-mediated rather than a public test download. Formal publication evidence [site-a11p-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 4886×921 (English) and 4885×921 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 4884×919 and 4883×919. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
